criterion: Each row of the problem list on the catalogue screen shows a status mark, a number with a title, a percentage to one decimal place and a difficulty word.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a catalogue row carries all four parts. Answer no when any one of them is missing from the row.

criterion: On the catalogue screen the three difficulty words wear teal for Easy, amber for Medium and red for Hard, each word dressed the same way beside its colour.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all three difficulty words carry their hue with one shared treatment. Answer no when a word is missing, a hue differs, or one band is dressed differently.

criterion: The catalogue control row carries a sort control, a filter control and a shuffle control beside the search field.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all three controls sit in the control row. Answer no when any one of them is absent.

criterion: Across tablet, desktop and widest widths the catalogue and workspace step through their tiers: an icon-only rail on a tablet, a labelled rail with a two-pane workspace on a desktop, right rails beside a centred column at the widest.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each of the three widths shows its described arrangement. Answer no when any width keeps the arrangement of another.

criterion: At a phone width the catalogue rail sits in a drawer behind a menu control, rows drop the frequency column, the workspace becomes a Problem and Code switcher, the price cards stack, and the streak, employer and topic panels reappear as a chip, a facet and a control.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the phone-width screens show each described change. Answer no when any one of them keeps its desktop form.

criterion: Opening a premium problem as a member lacking an entitlement shows a padlocked affordance carrying the price where the statement would sit on the workspace.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a padlocked affordance with a price stands in the statement area. Answer no when that area is blank, reports a missing page, or shows the statement.

criterion: A signed-out visitor opening the saved lists is sent to sign in and arrives back at the saved lists once signed in.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the visitor lands on the address first asked for. Answer no when the visitor lands on a home or dashboard screen instead.

criterion: A catalogue narrowed to a slice that returns nothing says so on the catalogue screen and offers to clear the narrowest facet.
evaluation_rule: A facet here is one of the topic, category, difficulty or status choices above the list. Answer yes when the empty result carries a message with a control removing one of those choices. Answer no when the list area is simply blank.

criterion: The verdict panel on the workspace moves from pending to judging to a single verdict, showing the runtime, the memory and both percentiles on an accepted one.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a settled submission shows one verdict with those figures after the pending and judging states. Answer no when two verdicts appear together or the figures are absent.

criterion: During loading the catalogue screen shows breathing placeholder rows at the height of a real row with a shimmer crossing unloaded blocks.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the loading state is row-shaped placeholders that pulse or shimmer. Answer no when the list area is empty or a lone spinner stands in for the rows.

criterion: The catalogue screen reads as a dense working list: compact rows, body-size text with smaller metadata, numbers aligned in columns, restrained elevation and more than one hue carrying meaning.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the catalogue shows each of those traits. Answer no when the list is spacious like a marketing page, the figures wander out of alignment, or one hue family dominates alone.

criterion: The catalogue screen, the workspace and the pricing route each lead with one primary action in a vivid blue, visually stronger than every secondary action beside that action.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a single blue action reads as the strongest on each of those three surfaces. Answer no when two actions carry equal strength or the primary action wears another hue.

criterion: Body text, difficulty labels and focus rings on the catalogue screen stand out from their background in both the light and the dark theme, with unavailable controls marked by more than colour.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when text and focus rings are readable in each theme and unavailable controls carry a second signal. Answer no when either theme leaves text faint or an unavailable control differs by colour alone.

criterion: The catalogue topic chip rail grows smoothly when Expand is pressed, and at a phone width the chip rail scrolls sideways snapping to chips with faded ends.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when both behaviours appear. Answer no when the rail jumps open or the phone-width rail wraps onto more lines instead of scrolling.

criterion: Contest ladder rows on the contest screen arrive one after another with a resolving blur, and toasts rise from below with one overshoot before leaving on opacity alone.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the ladder enters in sequence and a toast overshoots once on arrival. Answer no when the whole ladder appears at once or a toast slides away.

criterion: Topic tag names for an unsolved problem are readable on the workspace before the Topics disclosure is opened.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the tag names are readable without opening the disclosure. Answer no when the disclosure hides them until asked.

criterion: The oversized hero composition of the marketing route is repeated on the catalogue screen.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the catalogue opens on a hero band of the kind the marketing route uses. Answer no when the catalogue opens on its working list.
